result.markdown:
For most startups, I'd recommend **Linear** if you're building a tech or SaaS company, and **Notion** if you're looking for an all-in-one workspace.

The best project management tool isn't necessarily the one with the most features. It's the one your team will actually use consistently without spending more time managing tasks than doing the work.

Here are the tools I'd shortlist for a startup.

## Best project management tools for startups

![Projects – Linear Docs](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/H7btCzSbelKXdMr_2WS3GWddG9qajBq9JZDHM8HYyOoLV6E4HDh5vlzogddffE6t5gTnGdoZ53UsXuMyPZWPmHRUwQ3ddApfS44CKAri923rLMIeylRQs9HZxmyB23G0rTfX3tmbKwJPdUtZW_x9bJsI8X8b5_Xrbg_k3vvdE22XkcL7igbp9gCGi9QLirCv?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

- Excellent product and engineering workflows
- Issues, sprints, roadmaps and priorities
- Clean interface and fast adoption
- Great for teams shipping software

My first choice for a SaaS startup.

[Explore Linear](https://linear.app/)

**2\. ClickUp**

(Best all-in-one)

- Tasks, projects, docs and dashboards
- Automations and customizable workflows
- Useful across marketing, sales, product and operations
- Can become complex if overconfigured

[Explore ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![Project Management Hub Template by Gridvio | Notion Marketplace](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6e1oG6Y_aW5V5yDl222hE8Y8t-T__05L0OPLqrtY2b6KrmvS_M-QH4eaVLv4afPJUAGCFGr_eoifL-Irt3_HiUqUmKW08dRjhIxW2MfVWL_nPAWNaujkMp5zdq2VbJkW7b3h6jvrTVNAFmmVU9MPLCBztqWrhslDc_LeRhpbcV451et11onvlpgBLkBnIYcR?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage teams)

- Project management and company wiki
- Meeting notes, documentation and processes
- Flexible databases and task boards
- Requires some setup to create good workflows

[Explore Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Introducing Dashboards - a new way to see real-time project data in charts! - Product Launches - Asana Forum](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/wCWLFp4dMEl_v-oRmbowsFC6S4_evWBQMtRxSSXp7OXP6wtqD-ndySpIhbE0vKytZ9TUoZukBYXzktu332gBeqtOvFB5r_4mn9l1GOAEawsVNLrfaNRXIZhTP4IIa9xyWd0YUcL0lL-4dUI7q2c9LjUAelrs03KqyhIOzNbo8gDFWwNUhH6KJIHf5z_4WbFK?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

(Best for cross-functional teams)

- Clear task ownership and deadlines
- Project dependencies and timelines
- Good for coordinating departments
- More structured than some early startups need

[Explore Asana](https://asana.com/)

![Monday Vibe | Build Custom Apps with Vibe Coding & AI Prompts](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/dZbPOy2ExCYPWkRUN-y8aNBArPHAy5RJyF2Fv3kOH8r0onm7GzQMtNgFLnlF_orijMr1L_hlS3rZ5CmII7wcg1sC5QIg6R8JlCgddpaNU2x9UGq4FrFp6DOJXu4JvN0TyREqPyEMky1tg6L3RhInST4tHJiMa0BGxgH61Ibvrnb8NABR1soD10zbitKXa9pg?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

- Visual project tracking
- Good dashboards and automation

## My recommendation by startup type

| Startup situation | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| SaaS / technology | Linear |
| AI startup | Linear + Notion |
| General early-stage startup | ClickUp |
| Marketing / agency | Asana |
| Non-technical founding team | Notion |
| Operations-heavy startup | Monday.com |
| Very small team on a budget | Trello |


## What I'd actually implement

For a startup with 3–15 people, I'd keep the setup simple\:

- **Projects\:** One central project tracker.
- **Tasks\:** Every task has one owner and a deadline.
- **Priorities\:** Now, Next, Later.
- **Weekly planning\:** Agree on the three most important outcomes.
- **Company knowledge\:** Keep processes, meeting notes and decisions in Notion.

Avoid introducing five different tools when two will do.
